text:
maya: dropping a focused UX pass on min/max inputs, presets, and the SLO snap behavior. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/UXPASS/minmax-presets liam: good call. quick flag: numeric inputs + slider must stay perfectly in sync. if someone types a number we should update the slider without animation; on drag we can animate numbers. sara: copy suggestion: label the SLO control 'Latency target (99p)' and add small help text 'Adjust to prioritize latency or cost'. presets should be called 'Recommended profiles' not 'Presets'. ethan: accessibility: when a preset is applied announce it via aria-live: "Applied profile: Balanced. Estimated cost: $X (approx.)". also ensure slider tick marks are focusable and labeled for screen readers. olivia: product: presets should prefill min/max, SLO target, and quantization suggestion but not lock values. show a tiny badge "recommended" and an Undo affordance after apply. ben: burst UX: if user sets min==max, disable burst toggle and show tooltip 'Burst requires headroom: increase max to enable short spikes'. avoid allowing users to toggle something that has no effect. kelsey: mobile: numeric fields should be compact with +/- buttons and respect 44px touch targets. when screen is narrow collapse the summary row into stacked cards. maya: design question: should presets show an immediate diff in the top summary (cost delta / latency delta / peak)? I think yes, makes the impact clear. liam: agree. animation: animate numeric deltas with a count-up easing; but respect prefers-reduced-motion. sara: microcopy tweak for warnings: use 'may' and 'estimate' often. e.g., 'This change may increase 99p latency by ~12% (estimate).' ethan: dev note: debounce estimate calls when scrubbing slider (300ms). fire immediately on numeric input confirm. show skeleton state in summary cards while computing. olivia: guardrails: three tiers: info (ok), advisory (yellow, show suggestions), block (red, require changes). advisory should offer a suggested auto-fix button. ben: pool selector: show compact pool badges with name, free GPUs, and tier pill (low/med/high latency). disable presets that require pool features the selected pool lacks. kelsey: a11y nit: pool badges must have aria-labels like 'pool-a, 4 GPUs free, low latency' and keyboard focus styles. maya: visual: top summary row with three mini-cards (cost, latency, pool). clicking a card expands details below. keep modal height constrained. liam: QA scenarios: min>max typed, min==max + burst toggle attempt, applying preset then editing, switching pools mid-edit, and reduced-motion preference. sara: copy for CTA: primary 'Apply capacity changes' secondary 'Preview in console'. after apply show an undo toast for 90 seconds. ethan: snippet for aria-live included in figma comments:
Applied profile: Balanced. Estimated monthly cost: $12.40 (approx.)
olivia: telemetry: capture preset id, assumptions snapshot (tokens/hr, seq len, pricing), and selected pool when a change is applied for audit and regressions. ben: implementation: if pool doesn't support burst, show 'Burst not available on selected pool' inline and auto-disable the toggle. kelsey: mobile overflow: make presets horizontally scrollable with pagination dots, or collapse into an overflow menu. maya: action items: sara -> finalize copy for presets/tooltips/CTA; liam+ethan -> sync slider+numeric behavior + debounce; ben+kelsey -> pool badge + mobile behavior; olivia -> telemetry spec; maya -> update figma and add acceptance criteria. deploy-bot: uploaded asset -> minmax-presets-v1.png maya: thanks all 44d. aiming to ship prototype to staging by EOD Wed. ping in thread with any follow-ups or accessibility test results.
